 ## `argmix test`
 
 - Reports SNP-level accuracy and soft `r2` (probability-weighted ancestry dose against true dose) for one evaluation replicate.
-- Defaults to the first test replicate and falls back to the first validation replicate when `test_replicates` is empty; `--split val|test` forces one. The fallback prints a warning, because early stopping already picked the checkpoint on the validation replicate, which makes an accuracy measured there optimistic.

 ## Checkpoints
 
 `argmix train` does not reuse an existing checkpoint unless you pass `--reuse-compatible-checkpoint`, and `--force` overrides that flag to train from scratch.
 
-`argmix test` selects its checkpoint in this order: `--base-checkpoint`, then `runtime.base_checkpoint`, then `models/checkpoints/latest_checkpoint.path`, then the newest `*/best_model.pt`. `runtime.base_checkpoint` only chooses which checkpoint to evaluate; it does not initialize training weights.

 ## `argmix infer`
 
-`argmix infer` scores an ARG you built with Relate yourself, outside the project pipeline. It takes explicit paths (`--trees`, `--references`, `--recomb-map`, `--checkpoint`, `--predict-pops`, `--relate-sample`) rather than a manifest split, so no project config is involved. `--predict-pops` only selects which nodes to score; the output ancestry classes come from the checkpoint. For the full flag list, the node-metadata schema, and worked examples see the [HGDP guide](../guides/hgdp_1kgp.md#using-argmix-infer).
